title: Proposals For Comment
summary: This Federal Reserve Board webpage is a listing page aggregating multiple active regulatory proposals open for public comment. Among the proposals, two are market-structure relevant: (1) FedNow Service amendments to allow intermediaries for cross-border payments (R-1891, comments due 06/09/2026), and (2) GSIB capital surcharge revisions including modifications to wholesale funding measurement and reduction of cliff effects (R-1889, comments due 06/18/2026). The remaining proposals focus on regulatory capital rules for banking organizations. As a listing page aggregating multiple distinct proposals, this source is not suitable for individual archival; each proposal would need to be accessed via its specific link for proper documentation.
key_points: PAGE_TYPE is listing_page — source is non-archiveable per system rules; individual proposals must be accessed separately.
FedNow proposal (R-1891): would permit FedNow participants to use private-sector intermediaries for cross-border transactions, using FedNow for U.S. domestic leg.
GSIB surcharge proposal (R-1889): modifies method 2 coefficients, switches certain single-date measurements to average values, and reduces cliff effects.
Additional capital-related proposals (R-1888, R-1887, R-1876) address standardized approach risk weights and Category I/II organization capital requirements.
Proposal R-1884 addresses reputational risk removal from supervisory programs; comments due 04/27/2026 — earliest deadline.
All proposals are open for public comment; no decisions have been made or implemented.
why_it_matters: Regulatory capital proposals affect how banks calculate capital requirements, influencing lending capacity and risk-taking incentives. The GSIB surcharge revisions could alter systemic risk incentives for the largest banks. FedNow amendments could expand cross-border payment infrastructure.
market_structure_context: FedNow proposal (R-1891) relates to payment system infrastructure by enabling private intermediaries for cross-border transactions. GSIB surcharge revisions (R-1889) relate to market structure by affecting how systemic risk is measured and penalized for the largest banks.
